answer.E: The proportion of anxiety caused by social media marketing (43.8%) is close to the proportion of poor sales impression of traditional gyms (39.9%), proving that the aversion to social media is the dominant driving force.
answer.F: The high proportion of pain points of sub - health status and chronic diseases, combined with the dissatisfaction with the coaching ability and course homogenization of traditional gyms, may explain users' preference for personalized or health - management - oriented alternative methods.

Please select the most reasonable strategic suggestion.

answer.A: Since the online fitness penetration rate soared from 0% in 2015 to 45.5% in 2021, the traditional gym model should be completely abandoned, and all resources should be transferred to online platforms to meet users' full - scale digital needs.
answer.B: Focus on investing in the development and promotion of online fitness platforms. The residents' health literacy shows a continuous upward trend, and the popularity of online fitness methods has increased rapidly. This indicates that online channels have become an efficient way for residents to adopt healthy behaviors. In response to the high - incidence pain points of fitness users, such as less free time and bad living habits, online platforms can provide flexible and accessible solutions, thus maximizing the efficiency of resource utilization.
answer.C: Strengthen special intervention projects targeting work - life stress and emotional health. The pain points related to work - life stress among fitness users have the highest proportion, and the data on the literacy of healthy lifestyle shows obvious fluctuations in some years. Resource allocation should give priority to alleviating these stress sources. Through mental health services and education, the stability of overall healthy behaviors can be improved, avoiding focusing only on physical exercise.
answer.D: Given that the literacy level of healthy lifestyle and behavior decreased from 10.3% in 2015 to 9.8% in 2016, the resource investment in behavior intervention projects should be reduced to avoid waste in areas with high volatility.
answer.E: Strengthen the construction of basic medical facilities, such as increasing the number of hospital beds and clinics, because all health problems ultimately require professional medical intervention.
answer.F: Promote the reform of the traditional gym service model and integrate online advantages. Among the reasons for not choosing traditional gyms, the high risk of the annual card model and the lack of time flexibility account for a relatively high proportion. Combining with the significant growth trend of online fitness penetration rate, policies should encourage gyms to provide hybrid models (such as short - term memberships or digital courses) to address users' concerns and expand the coverage.
answer.G: Promote a national healthy diet and exercise program, and publicize healthy recipes through the media as a basic means to improve lifestyle.

qa_pairs.question: Based on the main pain points of fitness users and the reasons for not choosing traditional gyms, how should gym operators adjust their service strategies to improve user attraction and retention rates? Please select the most effective suggestions.

answer.A: Integrate mental health and social elements into fitness courses. The pain points related to work stress and narrow social circles among fitness users account for a significant proportion, and the problem of homogenized courses is prominent among the reasons for not choosing traditional gyms. The strategy should develop diversified courses (such as stress - relief group activities) to address in - depth needs and achieve differentiated competition.
answer.B: Increase brand advertising investment through TV and social media to enhance brand awareness and attract more potential users.
answer.C: Since the proportion of users dissatisfied with the coach's teaching attitude and ability is as high as 43.0%, the cost of coaches should be significantly reduced, and AI tutorials or low - paid part - time coaches should be used instead to improve operational efficiency.
answer.D: Introduce a flexible membership system (such as monthly cards or pay - per - use) and reduce the frequency of sales promotion. Among the reasons for not choosing gyms, the long - term annual card model and the negative impression of sales promotion account for a relatively high proportion. At the same time, the pain points of less free time and income constraints among fitness users are prominent. A flexible payment and low - interference service can directly improve the user experience and affordability.
answer.E: Provide free fitness equipment trials or discount vouchers as a common marketing means to encourage new users to join.
answer.F: Given that the pain point of difficulty in balancing work and life accounts for 39.9%, the gym opening hours should be extended to 24 hours to ensure that all users can access the gym at any time, solving the problem of less free time.
answer.G: Upgrade coach training and store environment design, focusing on personalized services. User dissatisfaction with coach ability and store attractiveness is a major obstacle. Combining with the high - incidence pain points of dissatisfaction with one's own body and chronic diseases among fitness users, high - quality coaches and a modern environment can provide customized guidance, enhancing trust and satisfaction.

answer.B: Strengthen community projects for chronic disease prevention and life stress management. The pain points of sub - health status and emotional stress among fitness users are prominent, and the data on the literacy of healthy lifestyle shows slow growth in the early stage. Resources should be tilted towards grass - roots interventions (such as free screenings and stress workshops) to focus on prevention and improve the stability of literacy.
answer.C: Organize community health lectures and free medical consultations to popularize basic medical knowledge as a common method to enhance health awareness.
answer.D: Increase emergency funds for public health events, such as the reserve of epidemic prevention supplies, because sudden events are the main source of health risks.
answer.E: Give priority to funding online health education and fitness projects to expand the coverage. The residents' health literacy shows a continuous upward trend, and the popularity of online fitness has increased rapidly, indicating the high efficiency of digital channels. In response to the pain points of social media anxiety and bad habits among fitness users, online projects can reach a wide range of people at low cost, especially those with limited time or income.
answer.F: Since the literacy level of healthy lifestyle and behavior increased from 19.2% in 2019 to 26.4% in 2020, resources should be concentrated to replicate the strategies in 2020 (such as online fitness) because the results were the most significant that year.
answer.G: Promote policy supervision of the gym industry to reduce users' risk perception. Among the reasons for not choosing gyms, the concerns about merchants running away and dissatisfaction with prices account for a relatively high proportion. Combining with the increasing trend of online fitness penetration rate, government intervention (such as a deposit system) can enhance trust, promote the integration of traditional and online models, and improve the overall credibility of the industry.
